To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“During mitotic exit, chromosomes that fail to segregate correctly fail to assemble a complete nuclear envelope, which leads to spontaneous nuclear envelope rupture and genome instability.”

(1) the architecture of the nuclear envelope is disrupted in micronuclei, (2) this disruption is caused by defective nuclear envelope assembly on lagging chromosomes during mitotic exit and (3) spindle microtubule attachment blocks assembly of non-core nuclear envelope components, such as the nuclear pore complex, and causes the irreversible defect in nuclear assembly.
micronuclei fail in nuclear envelope assembly, and that this failure is a direct consequence of the mitotic spindle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the assembly of the nuclear envelope.
the mechanisms by which the nucleus and its envelope is assembled and maintained during cell division.
the assembly of the nuclear envelope during the final stage of cell division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“Nuclear envelope assembly is defective during mitotic exit, leading to spontaneous nuclear envelope disruption of micronucli and subsequent genome instability.”
the mitotic spindle prevents the normal assembly of the nuclear envelope, and this leads to spontaneous nuclear envelope disruption of micronucli and genome instability.
the mitotic spindle prevents proper nuclear envelope assembly in micronuclei, leading to spontaneous nuclear envelope disruption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitotic spindle prevents the normal assembly of non-core nuclear envelope components on missegregated lagging chromosomes, which leads to spontaneous disruption of micronucleus nuclear envelopes.
the nuclear envelope assembly is a dynamic process that is tightly coordinated with mitotic spindle disassembling.
the nuclear envelope is not a static entity, but rather a dynamic structure, whose assembly and disassembly are tightly coordinated with cell cycle progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the timing of nuclear envelope assembly and chromosome segregation during mitotic exit is not precisely coordinated, and that errors in the assembly of the nuclear envelope can lead to micronucleus formation and subsequent genome instability.
micronuclei have an inherent fragility that arises from the failure to assemble a normal nuclear envelope.
the timing of nuclear envelope assembly during mitosis is not precisely controlled, such that missegregated chromosomes are not properly incorporated into the nucleus during mitotic exit.
